objective: Demonstrate automatic extraction, compilation and deterministic reuse of a mechanical API verification recipe before generalizing extraction.

attempts.goal: Create a small, dependency-free Node verification package for local HTTP APIs. Its public command is `node replay.mjs <manifest.json>`. The JSON manifest supplies a workspace-relative Node server entry and an ordered list of GET requests with paths, expected status codes and expected JSON bodies. The CLI launches that server on an OS-assigned 127.0.0.1 port, compares each observed status and parsed JSON body structurally, and always stops the server. It prints exactly `<N> checks passed\n` and exits 0 only when every check matches; malformed input, a missing server, timeout or any mismatch must produce a diagnostic and a nonzero exit. Include a tiny local sample API (GET /health -> 200 {"ok":true}; GET /double?n=7 -> 200 {"value":14}; GET /missing -> 404 {"error":"not_found"}), a passing manifest, and a deliberately incorrect expected-body manifest that demonstrates the nonzero path. Preserve ordered request semantics and never rewrite expected values to make checks pass. Include the machine-readable .atoma-probes.json version 1 recording the actual command invocations and their observed exit/stdout/stderr. No UI, external networking, dependencies or package installation.
